findings.statement: Quant Battle (easy): fixed 120s blitz phase that never ends early, then up to 480s for 4 tactical questions; worst case 10 min per match.
Quant Battle (medium): fixed 120s blitz phase that never ends early, then up to 600s for 4 tactical questions; worst case 12 min per match.
Quant Battle (hard): fixed 120s blitz phase that never ends early, then up to 720s for 4 tactical questions; worst case 14 min per match.
Bot battles (easy, tech/IB): after a wrong or non-perfect submission the player waits for the bot's simulated finish, uniformly 35-85s after match start, with no interaction available.
Bot battles (medium, tech/IB): after a wrong or non-perfect submission the player waits for the bot's simulated finish, uniformly 65-140s after match start, with no interaction available.
Bot battles (hard, tech/IB): after a wrong or non-perfect submission the player waits for the bot's simulated finish, uniformly 100-230s after match start, with no interaction available.
Matchmaking falls back to a bot after 3s, so most battles are likely against bots. battle_started does not record opponent type, so GA4 cannot confirm this.
Optiver 80-in-8: 80 questions in 8 min; the run only ends at the timer or after the final question.
The matches table only records games where both players have accounts (including bots); guest games leave no server trace, and no match duration is stored.
battle_started only carries [category, difficulty, game_session_id, is_quant_battle, opponent_type, queueStartedAt, queue_ms]: no category, difficulty, opponent type or queue time.
Question bank: 279 questions. Audit flags: duplicate_title=8, tolerance_very_loose=3, heavy_reading_for_tier=3, no_rounding_instruction=11. 0 high-severity.
11 numeric questions have a 3+ decimal answer but no rounding/unit instruction (e.g. qm46, qm47, qm49, qm52); correct answers in another unit or precision may be marked wrong.
8 questions reuse another question's title across tiers (e.g. tm1, tm3, th8).
IB battle pools hold 3 questions per tier and each match draws 3: every IB match serves the identical question set.

data.title: Dead waiting time in bot battles
data.observation: After a wrong or imperfect submission in tech/IB bot battles, the player must wait for the bot's simulated finish (up to ~4 minutes on hard) with nothing to do. Matchmaking falls back to bots after 3s, so this likely affects most battles.
data.hypothesis: Players who finish before the bot leave during the non-interactive wait, lowering battle completion and replay.
data.intervention: When the human has finished, resolve the bot's (already simulated) result immediately and show the result screen. Outcome probabilities are unchanged.
data.causalStatus: untested: supported by code inspection and correlational data only

data.title: Ambiguous answer format in numeric questions
data.observation: Several numeric questions expect a rounded decimal (or a specific unit) without saying so; tolerance-based grading can then reject correct reasoning.
data.hypothesis: Players who get a "wrong" verdict on a correct-but-differently-formatted answer feel cheated and abandon the game or stop trusting the bank.
data.intervention: Show reviewed, clarified wording (explicit unit and rounding) for the flagged questions.
data.causalStatus: untested: supported by code inspection and correlational data only

data.title: Quant Battle is long and its blitz never ends early
data.observation: A Quant Battle is a fixed 120s blitz followed by up to 8-12 minutes for four tactical questions (worst case 10-14 minutes).
data.hypothesis: The match length exceeds what casual visitors budget for, so a share leave before the result screen, especially on mobile.
data.intervention: Test a shorter format (e.g. 60s blitz and a 6-minute tactical cap) once duration data shows how often players run to the limit.
data.causalStatus: untested: supported by code inspection and correlational data only

data.title: IB battles always serve the same three questions
data.observation: Each IB tier has exactly as many questions as a match draws, so every IB match repeats the identical set.
data.hypothesis: Returning players see no novelty in IB battles and stop replaying them; this depresses repeat play for that segment.
data.intervention: Expand IB pools (at least 15 per tier) before any experiment; meanwhile, hide IB battles or label them as a fixed set.
data.causalStatus: untested: supported by code inspection and correlational data only

outline: server/index.js startBotMatch: keep the bot resolution in a named function; in the treatment arm call it (and clear the pending timers) from submit_answer once the human has finished.
socket auth: accept anonId in handshake auth; server computes the variant with agent/src/flags/assign.js (same file served to the client as /flags.js).
match_found payload: include { experiment_id, variant } so the client can fire experiment_exposure once.
Default to control whenever the experiment is not live (unapproved, edited after approval, or missing anonId).
server/question-clarifications.js: map of question_id -> reviewed clarification text (drafted by the agent, approved by a human).
Serve clarified descriptions to treatment units in /api/questions and buildTacticalSet; control receives the original text.
question_presented carries { question_id, affected: true|false, variant } so analysis can restrict to affected questions.
Persist /api/flag into a question_flags table so the dispute guardrail is measurable.
